records.abstract: A systematic review and meta-analysis identified 13 randomized trials involving 403 healthy adults, evaluating transcranial random noise stimulation and cognitive outcomes. The pooled effect was small and not statistically significant (Hedges g 0.17; 95% CI -0.06 to 0.40; p=0.145). Online-stimulation subgroup estimates were positive, but the between-subgroup difference was not statistically significant. Other tested cognitive domains and stimulation parameters showed no clear significant differences. The authors concluded that current evidence remains limited and uncertain and called for larger standardized trials.
